trust_decision.summary: Whether a decoder-created view (DataView / Uint8Array on decoder.arr.buffer) stays inside the bytes of decoder.arr; decided (absent) in readFromDataView, present in readUint8Array, and indirectly by whether fromBase64 returns a view on Node's shared Buffer pool.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names `readFromDataView`; it builds `new DataView(decoder.arr.buffer, byteOffset + pos, len)` with no length/position check against decoder.arr.

fix_sites.entry_point: decoding.readFromDataView / readFloat32 / readFloat64 / readBigInt64 / readBigUint64 / readAny (cases 124,123,122) / buffer.decodeAny
decoding.readUint8Array / readVarUint8Array / readTailAsUint8Array / readVarString (native) / readAny case 116
fix_sites.module_kind: core binary decoder (refactor onto shared helper; check already present at decoding.js:106)

fix_sites.entry_point: buffer.fromBase64 / buffer.fromBase64UrlEncoded (Node build), reached by crypto/jwt.js:16 and crypto/jwt.js:44
fix_sites.module_kind: utility / base64 deserializer producing decoder input (separate module)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: buffer.js:75-78 (fromBase64Node returns a view on Node's pooled Buffer, so its .buffer and any unchecked view reach unrelated pool memory)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: fromBase64Node returns exactly the decoded bytes (buf.byteOffset/byteLength are correct), so a solver can argue it is not an out-of-bounds read and that the decoder fix alone closes the CVE; the zero-copy view is also an intentional performance idiom used elsewhere (decoding.js:96-97).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: readUint8Array must keep returning a zero-copy view sharing the parent ArrayBuffer (documented; a test reads `.buffer` of the result), must accept len 0 at end of data and decoders over sub-views with non-zero byteOffset; a fix that copies, or rejects non-zero byteOffset, or validates against arr.buffer.byteLength instead of arr.length breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: decoder.arr is a sub-view with non-zero byteOffset of a larger ArrayBuffer (fix.diff:50-51)
decoder.pos already past end (readUint8 increments pos unchecked, decoding.js:149) or set via clone(decoder, newPos) (decoding.js:87-91)
Node pooled Buffer from base64 decode (fix.diff:67-71)

O7_producer.where: buffer.js:75-78 (fromBase64Node, base64 decode producing pool-backed Uint8Array)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a peekFloat64/peekFromDataView or readUint16Array/readFloat64Array helper building a typed-array/DataView on decoder.arr.buffer without the new subdataview check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the module already has paired read*/peek* functions (decoding.js:209-236, 314-333) and builds views directly on .buffer for performance

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Node-only helper returning a Node Buffer (or a Uint8Array view over buf.buffer) that is then fed to a decoder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the .node.js variants wrap Node APIs that return Buffers, mirroring fromBase64Node's view-over-pool idiom

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Node decodeUtf8/encodeUtf8 fast path using Buffer.from(...) and re-wrapping buf.buffer as a view
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same Buffer-to-Uint8Array conversion pattern as buffer.js:76-77 for speed

O9_family: out-of-bounds read / information exposure via typed-array view outside the source view (CWE-125)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm; tests via `node ./test.js` under c8 (package.json:524)
O10_build.project_tests: buffer.test.js and encoding.test.js (round-trip any/uint8Array/float encodings, encoding.test.js:477, encoding.test.js:547-564)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (len > decoder.arr.length - decoder.pos) throw` to readFromDataView only, leaving fromBase64Node returning a pool-backed view.

out_of_scope_notes: readUint8/readUint16/readUint32/peek* (decoding.js:149-236) read past the end as undefined via bounded typed-array indexing; not a memory over-read, not pursued.
encoding.writeOnDataView (encoding.js:456-461) builds a DataView on the encoder's own buffer after verifyLen; write side, not pursued.
